purpose: Current IAMAI visual comparison/reference pack. Canonical HTML continues to own application anatomy; these files own the approved visual skin used for rendered comparison.

logo.$comment: Identity and provenance only. The measurements live once, in the `logo` block at the foot of this file, which is read off iamai-threshold-master.svg. An earlier iteration repeated a DIFFERENT set of numbers here (32-unit panels, a 36-unit gap, y32/y91/y24); those were stale and are removed, because a second copy of a measurement is the thing that lets a redraw look approved.
logo.name: Threshold
logo.geometry: see the `logo` block at the foot of this file

globalRulings.statusPills: primary-text words + semantic dot; state must never be color-only
globalRulings.derivedColors: may derive from core roles but may not introduce independent brand/semantic hues
globalRulings.planCollapsedRows: transparent hairline-separated rows inside phase grouping; opened row becomes the attached surface-backed header

repositoryIntegration.designAuthorityManifestChange: dark name -> Blue Slate; logo direction -> Threshold
repositoryIntegration.rendererRuling: canonical HTML remains anatomy authority; rendered visual comparison target uses the derived approved references
repositoryIntegration.testsNote: tests that byte-pin Deep Mineral or Guided Route must be updated to Blue Slate and Threshold

planOrganization.$comment: The final Plan BOARD organisation authority. It is recorded separately from the `files` hash because its authority is narrow and the boundary is the point: two Plan references are current at once and a later task must be able to read which owns what, as a value rather than by opening both.
owns: collapsed roadmap rows and the column head
Needs attention / Up next focus controls
planOrganization.expandedStepAuthorityNote: The two files own different halves of the Plan: this one owns the board, and the step-variants reference owns what a row opens into. See `planStep` below, which also records where it supersedes the older comparison reference.
planOrganization.exampleDataNote: The file carries design-example counts, dates, phase names and tenant facts. None of them is production data and none may be copied into production: docs/design/content.json remains the copy authority and the engine remains the fact authority.

planStep.$comment: The final EXPANDED-STEP visual authority. It is the other half of the Plan: iamai-plan-organization-final.html owns the board a step opens from, and this owns what opens. Recorded as its own block, with its own boundary, because two Plan references are current at once and a later task must be able to read which owns what as a value rather than by opening both and guessing.
planStep.$commentCurrentAuthority: Owner update, Sep 10, 2026: the expanded-step authority is docs/design/approved/anatomy/plan-step-v1.html as it exists on disk (sha256 below), which integrates Readiness and Implementation into every canonical variant, makes the right rail Next milestone only, and drops What IAMAI found, Who this touches and More from the step. iamai-plan-step-variants-final.html is superseded for the expanded step and is kept, unhashed-over, as the record of the previous design.
owns: the visual treatment of the step-family variants it draws
planStep.exampleDataNote: The file carries example people, counts, dates, tenant object names, policy facts and explanatory copy. None of it is production data and none may be copied into production: docs/design/content.json remains the copy authority and the engine remains the fact authority.

supersedes.$comment: Where the two disagree about expanded-step PRESENTATION, this file wins. The older reference is not deleted and its hash is not touched: it is the record of what the expanded step looked like before, and it is still the current authority for anything this file does not draw.
supersedes.remainsAuthoritativeFor: anything the step-variants reference does not draw

families.$comment: The reference draws six step families, and production now renders all six from it. `migrated` means the family goes through the ONE shared expanded-step frame with its optional modules gated by production truth — not that it has a renderer of its own. There is no per-family shell, which is the fact `src/ui/surfaces/stepFamilies.test.ts` holds the repository to.

familyModel.$comment: How a family is arrived at, so a later reader does not go looking for six components. `stepFamily` (src/ui/surfaces/stepContract.ts) is a READING and selects nothing: every optional module gates itself on the truth it needs, and the family is what you get when those gates resolve. Nothing reads a step's title.
modules: lifecycle track — where stepTrack finds a recorded lifecycle, never on a resolution step
Next caption — where the milestone has a dated line or a gate
Readiness — one to three tiles and the bar (stepContract.ts readinessOf); What IAMAI found and Who this touches are its evidence dialog
MFA preview and handoff — inside Readiness, where stepMfaHold names people
attention — the baseline-conflict notice and Fix before continuing, under Readiness
What to do — where the step has a decision, create lines or instructions of its own
decision primitive — where the content entry carries one
Implementation — Entra/PowerShell/JSON/AI Info from Foundation A and the translator, or the no-action box (implementationEmptyOf)
rail — Next milestone only, on every step (railOf)
footer — Exclude from rollout where the content entry marks the step excludable, Doesn't apply here where flagged, and the scan

planStep.implementedBy: plan shared step frame + policy rollout family pass; remaining families migrated by the final expanded-step pass

mfaReadiness.$comment: SUPERSEDED on 2026-09-19 (owner decision, docs/plans/2026-09-19-overnight-review.md item 22). This block recorded the Step 7 MFA Readiness visual and interaction authority. Prompt 62 replaced it with the v3 pack, which docs/design/approved/manifest.json records as the current MFA Readiness authority, and the owner's answer was to archive the old files. So the Step 7 reference and the two presentations it had superseded now live under archive/design/ as records; nothing current renders or tests from them. This block is kept so a later reader can see what the page answered to before, and where the authority went. Read the current authority from manifest.json, never from here.

the Plan gate and passkey rollout strip
worklist organisation: Person / Role / Methods / Proof / Readiness / Action
